picks.title: Run multiple AI image edits and keep designing while they load
picks.rationale: Official Figma release (Jul 7): parallel AI image edits without blocking the canvas — directly changes daily workflow; most actionable item in the pool.
picks.excerpt: Figma's Jul 7 release note: designers can now fire off multiple AI image edits simultaneously from the toolbar and keep designing while they load — no more waiting for one edit to finish before starting the next. (Page dated 'Jul 7, 2026'; no per-entry permalink, entry title above.)

picks.title: Meta built an AI detection tool to ID images and video created with its new models
picks.rationale: New provenance layer for AI imagery: Meta's Content Seal watermark survives crops/screenshots but breaks C2PA/SynthID interop — a real issue for creative asset pipelines.
picks.excerpt: Meta previewed a web-based detector that reads Content Seal, the invisible watermark embedded in images made with its new Muse Image model (video via the upcoming Muse Video to follow). The mark survives cropping, compression and screenshots — but is incompatible with SynthID and C2PA Content Credentials, an interoperability headache for creatives.

picks.title: Trimble adds AI tools to MEP estimating software
picks.rationale: Concrete shipped AI in CAD/estimating: symbol counting from drawings cuts takeoff time 50-60% plus a natural-language assistant — measurable workflow change, credible trade outlet.
picks.excerpt: Trimble baked AI into its MEP estimating tools: automatic drawing-scale/naming detection, AI symbol counting from construction drawings (3M+ symbols auto-detected, manual takeoff time cut 50-60%), auto-routed conduit length takeoff, and a natural-language AI Smart Assistant in Accubid Anywhere (80%+ time saved on historical-pricing research).

picks.title: Own the loop: how designers and researchers win with AI evals ft. Setor Zilevu (Figma) | Config 2026
picks.rationale: Most designer-actionable of the three fresh Config 2026 uploads: why design/research should own AI evaluation loops — a skill shift, not a rehash; 1 of max 2 allowed from this outlet.
picks.excerpt: Freshly uploaded Config 2026 session: Figma's Setor Zilevu on why designers and researchers should own the AI evaluation loop — using evals as the design instrument that shapes the quality of model-powered products.

picks.title: Subscription now required for longer access to some Meta glasses features
picks.rationale: Fresh platform-policy news: AI generation allowances and reasoning mode on Meta glasses move behind a $20/mo tier — affects anyone prototyping for the device; adds vr category and a 5th outlet.
picks.excerpt: Meta now gates longer use of some smart-glasses features behind the $20/mo Meta One Premium subscription — including bigger monthly AI usage allowances, more image/video generations with advanced models, and 'Thinking' mode reasoning. Free users get 3 hours of Conversation Focus vs 15 for subscribers, sparking criticism since the feature runs locally.
